key_impacts: Nuclear fuel melted inside the reactors due to the accident.
Coolant water became extremely contaminated and leaked into reactor building basements.
Around 400 tons of groundwater enter daily, filling the site with tanks of contaminated water.
Continuous cooling is required to prevent further radioactive releases.
evidence_snippets: Large-scale nuclear disaster at TEPCO's Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant, directly caused by the Great East Japan Earthquake and Tsunami of March 11, 2011.
Coolant water is circulated to cool the nuclear fuel that melted inside the nuclear reactors due to the accident.
Water becomes extremely contaminated, leaks into basements; about 400 tons of groundwater flow in daily, filling the site with tanks of contaminated water.
missing_information: Directly impacted settlements or exclusion-zone towns are not named.
Event timeline beyond the initial 2011-03-11 date is not detailed.
